condition: On corner lots, applies to the secondary street frontage for dual occupancy development (Part 3.3.2).
source_text: C.07 On corner lots, the secondary street setback must also be a minimum of 3 metres.
review_note: NEW. Part 3.3 heading is 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT DWELLING HOUSES, SECONDARY DWELLINGS AND DUAL OCCUPANCIES'; 3.3.2 is the dual occupancy sub-part. 'On corner lots, the secondary street setback must also be a minimum of 3 metres' - a minimum, so value_min is the requirement; no concession to strand in the condition; ground level; general to the LGA, not a precinct.

condition: On corner lots, applies to the secondary street frontage for secondary dwellings (Part 3.3.3).
source_text: C.09 On corner lots, the secondary street setback must setback a minimum of 3 metres.
review_note: NEW. 3.3.3 is the secondary dwellings sub-part of Part 3.3. Clause reads 'On corner lots, the secondary street setback must setback a minimum of 3 metres' - the doubled verb is the document's own wording, not an extraction artifact. applicability secondary_dwelling_specific is right: it is the granny-flat control, not the house control.

condition: Manor houses (Part 3.4.3, filed by the DCP under Multi-Dwelling Housing). On corner lots, to the secondary street frontage.
source_text: C.06 On corner lots, the secondary street setback must be a minimum of 3 metres.
review_note: NEW, and the dev_type was WRONG in a way that would have served a contradiction. The page states 'manor houses shall be a maximum of 2-storeys', so this clause's subject is manor houses - but it sits under the MULTI-DWELLING HOUSING heading and was proposed as dev_type multi_dwelling_housing at 3m. Parramatta already serves multi_dwelling_housing at 4m. Two rows, one dev_type, 4m and 3m, with nothing in dev_type to tell them apart. Corrected to dev_type manor_house, which is the clause's own subject and an existing value in the table's vocabulary. No number changed.

condition: Applies to apartment buildings on corner lots, to the secondary street or laneway frontage (Part 3.5.1).
source_text:
C.04 Buildings must be set back a minimum of 3 metres from the secondary street or laneway
frontage to support an adequate threshold to ground floor apartments and boundary
landscaping.
review_note: NEW. Page heading 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT APARTMENT BUILDINGS', part 3.5.1. 'Buildings must be set back a minimum of 3 metres from the secondary street or laneway frontage'. GRAIN checked: this is the building setback, not an upper-level massing control, and the clause's stated purpose (threshold to ground floor apartments, boundary landscaping) confirms ground level. 'or laneway' is in the condition, correctly - it widens what counts as the secondary frontage, it does not change the number.
